To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of RCA and/or FA in concrete is a sustainable practice in terms of both CIPR and EE.
the optimal solution of concrete mixes in terms of both EE and chloride ion resistance is the low w/b concrete with high volumes of recycled concrete aggregates (RCAs) and fly ash (FA).
the use of RCA in concrete is a good option to save EE.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the environmental impact and durability of concrete made with high volume of FA and RCA, and it can be used as a guideline for the selection of the most suitable concrete for the specific conditions of the project.

the environmental assessment of concrete made with high volumes of fly ash and RCA in terms of the EE and the chloride ion penetration resistance, which is a crucial factor in the service life of concrete.
the development of a sustainable concrete with high volumes of FA and RCA in the low w/b and the high w/b mixes, respectively, in terms of EE and CIPRs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the optimal solution is always the low and high w/bs with a high volume of RCA and FA.
it is always beneficial to use RCA and FA in the concrete mixes, especially in low w/b mixes.
it is better to use low w/b concrete with high volumes of FA and RCA, and the use of SP is recommended to enhance the CIPR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EE is not the only parameter to consider when designing concrete.
the concrete with high volume of FA and RCA, and with low w/b, is the best option to reduce the EE and improve the CIPR, which is in agreement with the results of previous studies.
the concrete containing both FA and RCA with low w/b and without SP, which is the most economical solution, is not the best in terms of the service life and the EE.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of RCA and FA in low w/b concrete is the best option for both EE and CIPP.
it is feasible to produce high-performance concrete with low EE and high CIPR.
the use of RCA in combination with FA is an effective strategy for reducing the EE and increasing the CIPR in concrete, especially when SP was used.
